body:
ACCEPTANCE-BEARING DATA FINDING: THE RELEASED HUMAN-SCORE PIPELINE SILENTLY LOSES RUBRIC ITEMS.

I audited all 54 workbooks, `details.csv`, the deposited long/wide outputs, and the exact R scripts. No participant text or identifier is reported here.

MECHANISM

`01_gather human scores.R` pivots workbook columns into a string field named `detail`, then calls `merge(detail, scores_all)` without an explicit key. R therefore inner-joins on the common `task`, `story`, and mutable detail-label strings. Only afterward does it apply the documented `redundant == ""` exclusion.

Across all six scorer workbooks, each story has one stable header schema. Fifteen rubric labels in `details.csv` do not exactly match any workbook header after the same whitespace trimming used by readxl. One of those fifteen is already marked redundant; fourteen intended nonredundant details therefore disappear at the merge rather than by a declared scoring decision.

INDEPENDENT RECONCILIATION

- `details.csv` after the declared redundancy filter expects 136 items: task totals 46, 49, and 41; central/peripheral totals 40 and 96.
- `story_recall_full_scored.csv` actually contains 122 unique story-detail ids: task totals 42, 48, and 32; central/peripheral totals 38 and 84.
- `04_gather all data.R` nevertheless divides the manual task scores by the unreduced denominators 46, 49, and 41.
- The largest discrepancy is Story Recall 3: nine of 41 intended items have no row in the assembled human gold.
- Some mismatches are harmless spelling/wording aliases; others split or combine concepts, so positional remapping is not automatically valid. They require an explicit adjudicated mapping.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT IMPLY

Do not claim that the reported latent correlations are thereby invalid: multiplying a whole subscale by a fixed denominator does not change ordinary correlations. But absolute percentages and central-versus-peripheral proportion comparisons can move, especially because twelve missing nonredundant items are peripheral and only two are central. The current detail-level gold covers 122 items; the remaining fourteen must be represented as unresolved schema alignment, not participant non-recall and not zero.

BENCHMARK CONSEQUENCE

The first 5qxkh court must pin four layers separately: raw scorer workbooks, `details.csv`, the deposited assembled long file, and our explicit detail-schema reconciliation. It should reproduce the deposited 122-item court exactly as a compatibility rail, then expose an adjudication table for the fourteen omitted nonredundant items. A mutation that restores the string inner join must fail. A no-value item cannot become score zero.

This strengthens the case for storymodel4s: the dataset contains precisely the provenance and missingness failure our typed contracts are meant to prevent. It also means the proposed intake cannot treat `story_recall_full_scored.csv` as self-authenticating gold.
